# Windows extended-display architecture

## Recommendation
Use a **same-origin dual-view session with a Window Management API role swap** in Edge/Chrome 100+ on Windows:

1. Start on a neutral setup/launcher surface, not a console-only page.
2. Preflight `window.screen.isExtended`; explain and request `getScreenDetails()` permission in a separate "Enable multi-display" step. Do not combine the permission prompt with final Start because the one-gesture launch assumes `ScreenDetails` is already available.
3. Let the presenter explicitly confirm **Audience display** and **Presenter display**. Default audience to a unique `isInternal === false` screen and presenter to `currentScreen`/the internal screen, but never assume OS `isPrimary` means laptop; show labels when there is ambiguity.
4. On the final **Start presentation** click, call `launcher.documentElement.requestFullscreen({screen: audienceScreen})`, then `window.open(consoleUrl, stableName, left/top/width/height from presenterScreen.avail*)`. The launcher becomes the public presentation and the popup becomes the private console.
5. Require a same-origin `CONSOLE_READY` handshake before declaring ACTIVE. If popup opening or handshake fails, close any partial popup and `exitFullscreen()` transactionally.

This is the standards-documented one-transient-activation sequence. The Window Management spec explicitly covers a slideshow on a projector with notes on a laptop and shows fullscreening the current document on one selected screen followed by opening a window on the other. It also contains a special activation waiver for the `window.open()` that follows target-screen fullscreen. [Window Management spec](https://w3c.github.io/window-management/#usage-overview-initiate-multi-screen-experiences), [Chrome Window Management guide](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/capabilities/web-apis/window-management)

Important consequence: **do not open the public child first and expect the opener's click to fullscreen that child.** Fullscreen activation belongs to the child document. If the product insists that the existing console remain the original window, use the viable two-step design: place/open the audience popup, then show a large "Enter fullscreen" control inside it. [Fullscreen request](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/requestFullscreen)

## Architecture boundaries and data flow
Keep this small; no distributed-window framework is justified.

- `DisplayCoordinator`: feature detection, permission state, `ScreenDetails`, screen selection, launch/rollback, and the state reducer below. This is the only module that knows browser display APIs.
- `PresentationSession`: canonical slide, animation/build step, timer, pause/hold, deck/version, and monotonically increasing sequence number. The launcher/audience owns authoritative state after launch.
- `/present/audience`: public renderer; setup launcher before Start, fullscreen public view after Start.
- `/present/console`: private controls, notes, next-slide preview, timing, and failure warnings.
- `BroadcastChannel(sessionId)`: commands console -> authority and authoritative snapshots/events authority -> all views. It works across same-origin windows. Because it has no retained messages, console sends `HELLO(lastSequence)` and audience replies with a full snapshot before `CONSOLE_READY`. [BroadcastChannel](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/BroadcastChannel)
- Keep the audience URL and console URL same-origin and do not navigate the console to untrusted content. A retained popup handle is useful for rollback and lifecycle checks. Note that adding `noopener` makes `window.open()` return `null`, so it conflicts with reliable block detection/handle monitoring; opener isolation would instead require relying entirely on the handshake and accepting the ambiguity. [window.open](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/open)

Listeners are event-driven: `screenschange`, each selected `ScreenDetailed.change`, `currentscreenchange`, permission `change`, `fullscreenchange`, `fullscreenerror`, `BroadcastChannel` messages, and popup unload/BYE. Do not poll. `ScreenDetails` is live; `screenschange` signals addition/removal but does not carry the new topology, so reread its `screens` array. [ScreenDetails events](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/ScreenDetails/screenschange_event), [ScreenDetailed](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/ScreenDetailed), [PermissionStatus change](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/PermissionStatus/change_event)

## Concrete state machine
```text
PROBING
  |-- API absent / insecure / denied --> MANUAL_SETUP
  |-- !isExtended --------------------> WAIT_EXTEND --screen change--> PROBING
  `-- supported ----------------------> WAIT_PERMISSION --granted--> SELECT_DISPLAY

SELECT_DISPLAY --screens chosen + listeners armed--> READY
READY --final Start click--> STARTING
STARTING
  |-- requestFullscreen reject/error --------> READY(error + retry/manual)
  |-- fullscreen ok + window.open returns null
  |       --> ROLLBACK(exitFullscreen) ------> READY(popup-blocked guidance)
  |-- popup opens but CONSOLE_READY absent
  |       --> ROLLBACK(close popup, exitFullscreen) --> READY
  `-- fullscreen + CONSOLE_READY ------------> ACTIVE_FULLSCREEN

ACTIVE_FULLSCREEN
  |-- fullscreenchange with null ------------> ACTIVE_WINDOWED
  |-- console BYE/closed ---------------------> HOLD_CONSOLE_LOST
  |-- audience screen missing on screenschange -> HOLD_DISPLAY_LOST
  |-- permission becomes denied -------------> HOLD_PERMISSION_LOST
  `-- Stop -----------------------------------> STOPPING

ACTIVE_WINDOWED --click inside audience: requestFullscreen--> ACTIVE_FULLSCREEN
HOLD_* --explicit recovery + fresh gesture--> SELECT_DISPLAY or READY
STOPPING --pause, exit fullscreen, close console, detach--> READY
MANUAL_SETUP --open audience from click; user drags + clicks fullscreen there
             --> ACTIVE_WINDOWED / ACTIVE_FULLSCREEN
```

`STARTING` is a transaction, not several independent optimistic effects. Do not advance the deck or start the clock until fullscreen and `CONSOLE_READY` both succeed.

## Failure handling

| Failure | Observable response | Recovery |
|---|---|---|
| Windows is duplicating / only one screen (`isExtended === false`) | Disable auto Start; show "Windows: Win+P -> Extend" | Re-probe on screen changes; never guess a second display |
| `getScreenDetails` absent | Manual setup | One direct-click `window.open`; user drags to projector and clicks fullscreen in audience window |
| Permission prompt/denial or `NotAllowedError` | Explain that access enumerates/places windows; show site-settings route | Continue manual; never dead-end the presentation |
| Popup blocked (`window.open()` null) | Exit fullscreen immediately; show allow-popups instructions and Retry | Stable named popup; one new window only per gesture. Browsers require direct input and one gesture per new window. [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/open#popup_blockers) |
| Fullscreen reject / `fullscreenerror` | Keep setup visible, do not open console | Retry from a fresh click or manual path. [fullscreenerror](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Document/fullscreenerror_event) |
| User presses Esc | Audience remains synchronized but windowed; console shows red "Audience not fullscreen" | Large re-enter control *inside the audience window* so its click supplies activation. [fullscreenchange](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Document/fullscreenchange_event) |
| Audience display unplugged / laptop lid closes | Freeze navigation and timer; preserve current public slide/hold frame | Rebuild picker from live topology; explicit Resume after selecting a valid audience display |
| Resolution, DPI, orientation, taskbar work area changes | Reflow renderer; update bounds/badges | No forced restart; `ScreenDetailed.change` covers these properties |
| Presenter moves a window deliberately | Update role/location badge | Do not continuously snap it back; `currentscreenchange` is observation, not authority to fight the user |
| Console closes/crashes | Audience shows current slide/hold, no autonomous advancing; timer pauses | "Reopen console" must be a fresh click; named target avoids duplicates |
| Permission revoked mid-session | Stop all automatic placement and show warning | Preserve current/manual output, require explicit re-enable |

Use `availLeft/availTop/availWidth/availHeight`, not `left/top/width/height`, for a normal console window so Windows taskbar/work area is respected. Virtual coordinates may be negative and the multi-screen origin is implementation-defined, so never derive "monitor 2 is +width to the right". [Window Management virtual arrangement](https://w3c.github.io/window-management/#concept-virtual-screen-arrangement)

## Strategy comparison

### A. Recommended: launcher -> audience fullscreen, console popup
- **UX:** one final Start gesture after permission/display preflight.
- **Coupling:** modest role transition in launcher; display API isolated.
- **Testability:** pure reducer + fake display adapter; real Edge/Chrome E2E for activation/placement.
- **Migration cost:** moderate because setup cannot be deeply console-specific.
- **Risk:** popup can still be blocked after fullscreen, hence mandatory rollback and handshake.

### B. Viable fallback: console stays, audience popup then second fullscreen click
- **UX:** two gestures and the second occurs on the projector surface.
- **Coupling/migration:** simplest ownership and lowest migration cost.
- **Reliability:** strongest cross-browser/manual floor.
- **Use:** always ship this fallback, and use it as primary if launcher role swap is unacceptable.

### C. Presentation API receiver/controller
- `PresentationRequest.start()` uses a UA display picker, needs transient activation, and provides connection state, messaging, reconnect, close, and terminate. It can run 1-UA remote-rendered or 2-UA receiver-device models. [Presentation API](https://www.w3.org/TR/presentation-api/), [MDN overview](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Presentation_API), [start security](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/PresentationRequest/start)
- It is **not** the best local attached-monitor fallback: it is experimental/non-Baseline, does not expose deterministic Windows topology/geometry, and introduces a separate receiver lifecycle.
- Keep it as a later, separate adapter only if Cast/TV/remote receivers become a real requirement. Do not mix its states into local window placement.

## Support and PWA implications
MDN browser-compat-data reports Window Management and target-screen fullscreen in Chrome 100+ with Edge mirroring Chromium; Firefox/Safari do not support them. Presentation API is Chrome 47+ / Edge mirror but unsupported by Firefox/Safari. Therefore Windows Edge/Chrome is the enhanced path and manual window + user fullscreen is the portability floor. [MDN BCD Window](https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/blob/main/api/Window.json), [ScreenDetails](https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/blob/main/api/ScreenDetails.json), [Element fullscreen options](https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/blob/main/api/Element.json)

Installing the PWA improves Windows affordances (app window, taskbar, Start, Alt+Tab, standalone chrome), but **does not bypass** HTTPS, Window Management permission, popup activation/blocking, or Fullscreen activation. Microsoft describes the same PWA front-end code running in-browser or installed; treat install as an optional rehearsal recommendation, never a capability gate. Detect standalone mode only to tune instructions/chrome. [Edge PWA architecture](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/progressive-web-apps/how-to/), [Windows PWA UX](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/progressive-web-apps/ux), [display-mode](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/display-mode)

`launch_handler` controls what an **OS launch** does with existing/new PWA clients; it does not place a presentation surface and should not own this flow. If configured, avoid `navigate-existing`, which could replace an active console; `focus-existing` or default behavior is safer, but this is orthogonal to `window.open`. [Chrome Launch Handler](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/web-platform/launch-handler/)

## Permission and security deployment rules
- HTTPS/secure context is mandatory. `window-management` Permissions Policy defaults to `self`; preserve that and do not delegate it to cross-origin frames. [getScreenDetails](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/getScreenDetails), [Permissions Policy](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Permissions-Policy/window-management)
- Query permission to tailor copy, but invoke `getScreenDetails()` to request it; Permissions API does not itself define prompting.
- Ask permission during setup, then arm final launch listeners before Start. Never request access on page load.
- Popup route must be same-origin, session-scoped, and unable to navigate to arbitrary URLs.
- Persist only a logical user preference (e.g. label/role hint), never trust stale coordinates or object identity after a topology change; require confirmation when labels/topology differ.

## Verification requirements for implementation
1. Real Windows Extended mode with laptop + HDMI projector, Edge current stable and Chrome current stable.
2. Installed PWA and ordinary browser tab; behavior must match except window chrome.
3. Projector left/right/above laptop, different DPI/scaling, taskbar on either display.
4. First-run permission grant, denial, revocation, popup block, Esc fullscreen exit.
5. Unplug/replug projector during setup, STARTING, and ACTIVE.
6. Multiple externals: explicit picker, never first-array-wins.
7. Console close/reopen, page reload/rejoin, and duplicate Start clicks; prove one console and monotonic state.
8. Firefox/manual path: popup from direct click, user drag, in-window fullscreen control.
9. Assert visible behavior, not geometry API mocks alone: actual audience and console contents must be inspected on their respective Windows displays.
